summary: Environment permission drift causing ops-runner service account to be blocked for Private deploys in eu-west1
description:
Issue summary:
A recently automated policy normalization job (env-normalizer) appears to have applied a restrictive folder-level constraint which removed a necessary IAM binding for our ops-runner service identity. As a result the Dedicated/Private provisioning pipeline (ops-runner) is failing authorization checks when attempting to create/attach GCE instance templates and KMS keys for Private deployments in eu-west1.

Impact:
- Blocked Private deploys for multiple customers in eu-west1 using the dedicated provisioner.
- Provisioner API returns 403/AccessDenied when creating service resources.
- Manual retries fail until binding restored.

Environment:
- Prod: dedicated provisioning flow -> project: redwood-dedicated-eu-west1-prod
- Affected service account: infra-ops-runner@redwood-dedicated.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- Automation: infra/env-normalizer (scheduled job that enforces folder constraints)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger provisioning job for a Private deploy in eu-west1 (simulate minimal changes).
2) Observe failing calls in provisioner (logs show: iam.serviceAccounts.actAs denied; compute.instanceTemplates.create denied).
3) Inspect folder-level constraints with gcloud and compare current bindings to snapshot from 2026-03-10.

Observed behavior:
- Provisioner logs: repeated 403 with message "Permission iam.serviceAccounts.actAs denied on resource ..." and compute API 403 when creating instance templates.
- GCP IAM policy dump shows infra-ops-runner missing roles/iam.serviceAccountUser and roles/compute.instanceAdmin in the dedicated project.
- Audit logs correlate change to env-normalizer run at 2026-03-11T03:12:00Z which applied a deny constraint entry "restrict-external-roles" to the folder.

Expected behavior:
- env-normalizer should not remove necessary service bindings required by the provisioning pipeline; destructive changes should be blocked when they affect a known ops service identity.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Re-granted roles/iam.serviceAccountUser and roles/compute.instanceAdmin to infra-ops-runner for redwood-dedicated-eu-west1-prod via gcloud IAM patch at 2026-03-12T14:40:22Z.
- Kicked provisioner retries, which succeeded for one affected customer.

Next steps requested:
- Full audit of env-normalizer change set and rule evaluation to identify why bindings were removed.
- Add a whitelist / safe-scope to env-normalizer to skip known infra service accounts.
- Backfill any other folders/projects that lost bindings during the same window.
- Add a pre-change gating step (dry-run + owner notification) for folder-level deny constraints.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:10 - Ethan: pulled IAM policy history from folder llm-dedicated; found constraint insertion at 2026-03-11 03:12 by infra/env-normalizer job.

2026-03-12 10:05 - SRE (Marta Alvarez): matched audit log entries showing policy change and subsequent 403s from provisioner; ran gcloud iam policies get-iam-policy for project redwood-dedicated-eu-west1-prod and compared to 2026-03-10 snapshot.

2026-03-12 11:30 - Security (Omar V): initial hypothesis: env-normalizer's rule for removing 'broad roles' treated the ops-runner binding as noncompliant because the binding included a legacy group rather than a scoped service account tag.
2026-03-12 13:20 - Infra (Lena K): confirmed that terraform state had no recent change; env-normalizer is implementing changes directly via cloud resource manager API.

2026-03-13 08:00 - Ethan: ran a search across folders for other occurrences; found two other projects that lost the same binding pattern but were not actively used by provisioner (recorded for backfill).
comments: Priya Nair (2026-03-12): Observed multiple customer retries failing this morning. Blocking.—Assigned to @Ethan.
Ethan Morales (2026-03-12): Confirmed 403s. I restored the critical bindings as a stop-gap. Will continue investigation into env-normalizer rules and create PR to add safelist.
Marta Alvarez (SRE) (2026-03-12): Please also validate KMS roles — provisioner failed to create CMEK keys on first retry. I captured audit log snippets in Slack #internal-access.
Omar V (Security) (2026-03-13): Policy engine considered 'roles that reference broad groups' as removable. We need an allowlist pattern matching service-account emails to prevent infra breakage.

Lena K (Infra) (2026-03-14): Draft PR for env-normalizer safelist submitted: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1928. Includes dry-run flag for 48h and explicit skip for identities matching *.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
Ethan Morales (2026-03-14): Will run the dry-run in preprod across all folders and produce a delta report. Scheduling manual gate for changes touching folder 'llm-dedicated'.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Emergency restore of required bindings allowed provisioner to resume for impacted customers (manual gcloud patch).
2026-03-14: env-normalizer PR 1928 merged with safelist and dry-run gating. Dry-run to be executed for 48 hours in preprod before any folder-level deny constraint application in prod.
Follow-up actions assigned: add canonical list of infra service identities to central config (owner: Infra - Lena K), extend Confluence runbook with pre-change audit checklist (owner: SRE - Marta A).
